channel.title: Blockheight
channel.description: Blockheight reports crypto news: Bitcoin and Ethereum, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, regulation, security incidents and market structure.

item.title: Chainflip swap costs combine protocol, pool and network fees
item.description: Chainflip charges a 0.10% protocol fee plus pool and blockchain costs; the route, destination network and optional boost determine what a swap costs overall.

item.title: Solana DEX Tick Array Boundaries Shape Swap Execution
item.description: Solana tick arrays group pool ticks into accounts that swaps traverse in order; spacing and supplied arrays shape execution, price limits and route reliability.

item.title: How to Withdraw Part of a Concentrated Liquidity Position
item.description: A partial withdrawal removes a chosen share of a concentrated liquidity position, returning its current token mix while leaving the rest exposed to the pool.

item.title: How to Move Large Amounts Within Bridge Rate Limits
item.description: Large crypto transfers fit bridge rate limits when you check the route’s live cap, size each transfer within it and wait for capacity to refill before retrying.

item.title: Why refresh token metadata after a cross-chain transfer?
item.description: Refreshing token metadata after a bridge can correct a wallet’s symbol, decimals, logo or token listing, but it does not alter the asset or finish a transfer.

item.title: Blackhole LPs need gauge stakes to earn emissions
item.description: Blackhole pays $BLACK emissions only to liquidity staked in pool gauges; LPs should check pool votes, gauge eligibility and migration status before committing funds.

item.title: Token metadata gaps can mislabel assets and disrupt swaps
item.description: Token metadata gaps can hide or mislabel assets, distort displayed balances and complicate swap setup, while pool math still depends on contract addresses and raw token amounts.

item.title: How to Check Blackhole Swap Approvals Before Signing
item.description: Check the token, spender, network and allowance in a swap approval before signing; the requested amount helps show what a contract may be able to spend.

item.title: How to fund recurring USDC payouts on Base
item.description: Recurring USDC payouts on Base need a prefunded wallet, a scheduler that submits each transfer, and ETH for network fees; native USDC avoids token confusion.

item.title: Should You Add Liquidity or Hold Your Tokens?
item.description: Adding liquidity can earn trading fees, but it changes your exposure and may underperform holding; compare fees, price moves, costs and exit rules first.

item.title: How Arbitrage Pools Catch Up After a Price Move
item.description: Arbitrage trades move an automated market maker pool toward market price, while fees, liquidity and execution risk shape how quickly it catches up.

item.title: Why a TRON Energy delegation stays pending
item.description: A pending TRON Energy delegation can mean the transaction is unsigned, unconfirmed or not yet shown; check its hash and resource record before retrying.

item.title: Schedule TRON Wallet Transfers Around Energy Rentals
item.description: Send only after rented Energy appears in the wallet, and leave time before expiry to check the transfer, its resource use and the rental terms.

item.title: Why a Zero USDT Balance Raises TRON Transfer Energy
item.description: A USDT transfer on TRON uses more Energy when the recipient’s balance is zero because the contract creates a balance entry; demand can also shift estimates.

item.title: Gate XMR deposits before releasing payout
item.description: An XMR deposit should trigger payout only after the receiving wallet verifies its subaddress, amount and on-chain status; confirmation and spendability are separate gates.

item.title: How to diagnose a pending XMR bridge swap
item.description: A pending XMR bridge swap can sit at deposit confirmation, service processing or payout; match its IDs to each chain, check your Monero wallet, then escalate with evidence.

item.title: xmr bridge routes: choosing a path from your own wallet
item.description: Choose an xmr bridge route by matching the asset you hold to the destination coin and chain, then verify the receiving address and network before sending.

item.title: Why deeper cross-chain liquidity cuts swap slippage
item.description: Deeper swap pools reduce price impact by letting trades use a smaller share of available liquidity, but fees, routing and both chain legs still shape the quote.

item.title: Bungee Bridge routes: compare fees, slippage and output
item.description: Compare Bungee Bridge routes by the tokens delivered after fees, the minimum output allowed by slippage, network gas and timing—not by the lowest headline fee.

item.title: Treasury chart overlays show holdings beside price, with limits
item.description: A treasury overlay can show holdings beside token price, but balance changes, valuation and chart scales must be checked before reading it as a signal.
